Use case: ui-mockup. Asset type: 16:9 Google TV Battleship gameplay design concept, 1920x1080 composition. First reference is current native screen, other references are exact existing overhead ship art. Preserve dark navy ocean, subtle distant naval background, quiet text, cyan military circular reticle following a selected enemy cell, human captain portrait at top left and distinct female opponent captain at top right, turn label beside active captain. Two EQUAL large square 10x10 grids dominate lower center, enemy waters on left with NO intact enemy ship positions revealed, own visible ships on right. No bottom roster, no control instructions, no decorative labels, no extra menus. A tracker ABOVE EACH grid includes exactly five ship types ONCE each in this order: Carrier, Battleship, Cruiser, Submarine, Destroyer. Their silhouettes match existing ship art. On left each has ship picture plus ONLY Hidden or Sunk, no enemy damage or health pips. Show Carrier Hidden, Battleship Hidden, Cruiser Hidden, Submarine Hidden, Destroyer Sunk; a matching two-cell sunk wreck alone on enemy board. Own tracker has ship image and health pips 5,4,3,3,2 respectively; show carrier 5 intact, battleship 4 intact, cruiser 1 damaged and 2 intact, submarine 3 intact, destroyer Sunk. Distinguish damage by slash and color, never color alone. Intact pips gray, damage coral slashed; sunk picture dimmed with cross. Minimal readable type labels. Board geometry square, equal with same cell pitch, both grids as large as available space allows. No hidden positions or partial enemy damage shown in tracker. This is a screen design reference only, not a photograph or tablet frame.
CONCEPT A: Compact integrated horizontal strips. Above each grid, one continuous low-height strip of five tiny overhead ship thumbnails rotated horizontally, with short type label beside or underneath and status beneath. Flat layout without individual card boxes, thin separators only. Ship-art row and tiny status row, total tracker height approximately 65 pixels. Board labels sit just above strips. Keep all five entries readable, keep grids almost as large as existing native reference. Human portrait header at x100 y50, opponent at x1800 y50. All trackers align to board left/right edges. Quiet minimal design, board-first.
